# `voxel/ChunkSorter.js`

> **Source:** `engine/voxel/ChunkSorter.js`

ChunkSorter.js - Front-to-Back Chunk Sorting and Back-Face Culling Optimizations: 1. Front-to-Back Sorting: Render nearest chunks first for early-Z rejection 2. True Back-Face Culling: Skip entire face directions that point away from camera 3. Distance Culling: Skip chunks beyond render distance

## Classes

### `class ChunkSorter`

ChunkSorter - Manages chunk draw order and visibility

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor()` |  |
| `updateCamera` | `updateCamera(position, forward)` | Update camera state |
| `calculateVisibleFaces` | `calculateVisibleFaces(forward)` | Calculate which face directions are visible from camera A face is visible if it points toward the camera (dot product with -forward > 0) |
| `isFaceVisible` | `isFaceVisible(faceIndex)` | Check if a specific face direction is visible |
| `sortChunks` | `sortChunks(chunks)` | Sort chunks front-to-back by distance from camera Uses cascaded bucket sort for O(n) performance instead of O(n log n) |
| `iterate` | `* iterate()` | Get sorted chunks iterator |
| `getVisibleFaceCount` | `getVisibleFaceCount()` | Get visible face count (for statistics) |
| `getVisibleFaceNames` | `getVisibleFaceNames()` | Get visible face names |
| `getStats` | `getStats()` | Get statistics |

## Notes & Examples

### Voxel World System

The voxel system provides chunked 3D grids with fast access, mesh generation, and level-of-detail (LOD). Chunks are 32³ by default and stream in/out based on camera position. The mesher generates greedy or marching-cubes geometry depending on material.

**Example: Creating and modifying a voxel world**
```js
import { VoxelWorld } from 'engine/voxel/VoxelWorld.js';
import { VoxelMesher } from 'engine/voxel/VoxelMesher.js';

const world = new VoxelWorld({
  chunkSize: 32,
  loadDistance: 8  // chunks
});

// Set voxel at world position
world.setVoxel(10, 5, 10, {
  type: 'grass',
  color: [0.2, 0.7, 0.1]
});

world.setVoxel(10, 4, 10, { type: 'dirt' });

// Generate mesh for rendering
const mesher = new VoxelMesher(world);
const geometry = mesher.generateChunk(0, 0, 0);

// Raycast to find clicked voxel
const hit = world.raycast(rayOrigin, rayDir, 100);
if (hit) {
  world.setVoxel(hit.x, hit.y, hit.z, null);  // Remove
}
```
